title: Begusarai Fertilisers: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**A Begusarai fertiliser borrower is either a blending/warehousing unit or a wholesale/retail dealer, not a manufacturer.** Urea and complex fertiliser are made elsewhere and moved in by rail and road; local value-add is mixing, bagging, storage and last-mile credit to farmers. Cash comes in seasonally at Kharif and Rabi sowing, and the dealer carries stock and farmer receivables in between. **The working-capital cycle, not the plant, is where your money sits.**

## What has changed now
**The official data pack scores this sector-city pair at 20, well inside the avoid band [D].** Bihar GST collections are -0.1% Apr-to-date against India +6.1%, a 6.2 pp gap [D], and India-wide fertiliser output (NIC 20) is -0.5% YoY with -1.2% Apr-to-date [D]. Bank credit to the sector is +53.1% YoY against that -1.2% output [D] — so when a proposal lands, check whether the borrower's own sales growth matches its drawing-power growth; if the limit has grown faster than turnover, ask for the stock statement and sales register before any enhancement.

## Local news versus peers
**Local reporting is the weak spot and it is recent.** Retail vendors in Begusarai have opened a front against wholesalers over pricing [3], and a gas leak at a local fertiliser plant left a teacher unconscious for two hours, with management calling it a rumour [2]. A local piece also flags falling soil fertility from chemical fertiliser overuse [1]. Peer results are mixed and national, not local: Shree Pushkar's fertiliser revenue fell 10.6% YoY [4], while GSFC's fertiliser sales jumped 82% [5] and Deepak's margins rose from 16.8% to 21% [7]. CRISIL expects complex fertiliser capacity to rise ~25% over three fiscals on ~16 MTPA base [9]. **Sources say little about Begusarai specifically, so lean on first principles and these peers.**

## Who to pursue, who to avoid
**Pursue dealers with own godown, steady farmer relationships and sales booked against actual offtake.** The rating note on Fertis India is useful here: customised, less-regulated products sold across all four seasons reduce risk [8]. **Avoid pure price-arbitrage wholesalers** — the very group local retailers are protesting against [3] — and any unit near the plant named in the leak report until safety compliance is shown [2].

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the season, not the year.** Sanction a drawing power tied to paid stock and receivables, take monthly stock-and-receivable statements, and a quarterly GST return. Ask for the subsidy-claim position where applicable; collect from customer where the figure is missing.
